### Issue description

I would be surprised if this was not already reported, but I couldn't find an open issue talking about it, so just in case I'm making one myself.
My game typically has the mouse mode as MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED. In 4.7.2, and in 4.8 *on exported builds*, this works fine. However in the editor, it seems to instead be treating it as if it was MOUSE_MODE_HIDDEN instead, hiding the mouse but allowing it to exit the window.

orig.title: Subsequent serializations of empty arrays get their type overwritten
orig.body:
### Tested versions

v4.2.2.stable.official [15073afe3]
v4.3.rc2.official [3978628c6]
v4.7.dev3.official [60fff00a6]

### System information

Ubuntu

### Issue description

```
E 0:00:00:0552   assign: Cannot assign contents of "Array[int]" to "Array[String]".
  <C++ Error>    Method/function failed.
  <C++ Source>   core/variant/array.cpp:276 @ assign()
```

### Steps to reproduce

```swift
@tool
extends Control

var prop_a: Array[int]
var prop_b: Array[String]


func _get_property_list() -> Array[Dictionary]:
	var properties: Array[Dictionary]

	properties.append({
	   "name": "prop_a",
	   "type": TYPE_ARRAY,
	   "hint": PROPERTY_HINT_TYPE_STRING,
	   "hint_string": "%d:" % [TYPE_INT]})

	properties.append({
	   "name": "prop_b",
	   "type": TYPE_ARRAY,
	   "hint": PROPERTY_HINT_TYPE_STRING,
	   "hint_string": "%d:" % [TYPE_STRING]})

	return properties
```

Using `_get_property_list` we add two arrays of different types.

However, when these properties are serialized in the scene file, then `prop_b` will for some reason be given the same type as `prop_a`:

```
prop_a = Array[int]([])
prop_b = Array[int]([])
```

This then leads to the above error message at runtime. This appears to only happen when one or both of the arrays are empty.

Even when providing an empty array as default value via `_property_can_revert()` and `_property_get_revert()`, the empty array still gets serialized. Although perhaps that is a different bug.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[godot_4_property_array_bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16501163/godot_4_property_array_bug.zip)

### Godot version

4.0.beta3 / 3.5.1.stable

### System information

Arch Linux

### Issue description

When connected to `tree_entered`, built-in methods are always executed.

For example, connecting `Particle2D.set_emitting(true)` to its `tree_entered` signal will set emitting to true when I open the scene again. Connecting the signal to `queue_free()` crashes the editor when I open the scene again when using a saniziter build.

I'm not sure if this is intended.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new 2D scene.
2. Connect the root Node2D's `tree_entered` signal to its `queue_free` method.
    * Bring up the connection dialog.
    * Check "Advanced".
    * Select the Node2D node and type `queue_free` in Receiver Method.

dup.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.6.1.stable.official [14d19694e]

### System information

Godot v4.6.1.stable - macOS Unknown (27.0.0) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Metal (Mobile) - integrated Apple M5 (Apple9) - Apple M5 (10 threads) - 24.00 GiB memory

### Issue description

On my machine, the default editor display scale is `Auto (200%)`. I changed this to 175%.

In the text editor (word-wrap disabled), the horizontal scroll is sized to the longest line. But, it seems to scroll one character short, as it is not possible to see the last character. This issue does not occur on the default display scale, only after changing to a custom value.

200% - no issue
175% - issue
150% - issue
100% - partial issue. Last character is visible but partially obscured by the vertical scrollbar

### Steps to reproduce

1. In editor settings, change display scale to a fractional value (e.g. 150%, 175%).
  a. The specific value causing issue may vary by display
3. Restart the editor to apply changes.
4. Open a script in the Godot text editor.
5. Input a line of text longer than the visible width of the editor.

Expected behavior:
- As the user continues to type beyond the visible width, editor scrolls to show the final character and cursor.
- User can scroll horizontally to reveal the final character.

Actual behavior:
- Editor scrolls to show second-to-last character, cursor is out of view.
- User cannot scroll horizontally to reveal the final character.

dup.title: 4.8-dev5 consistently crashes on macOS during editor startup/initialization.
dup.body:
### Tested versions

-Consistently reproducible in v4.8.dev5.official [9552dfb68]
-Was not an issue in previous dev4 release.
-Possibly specific to macOS Metal renderer.


### System information

macOS 26.6.2, Mac Studio 2022 M1 Ultra, 64GB, 3 monitor setup.

### Issue description

4.8-dev5 launches into the project selector window fine, but consistently crashes when trying to open an existing project or create a new one.  According to crash logs, the faulting instruction is:

> OffsetAllocator::Allocator::free(OffsetAllocator::Allocation)

CPU exception:

> EXC_BAD_ACCESS
> SIGBUS
> KERN_PROTECTION_FAILURE

Looks like it's trying to access an address on the Metal heap.

Launching this version of Godot from Terminal using rendering method gl_compatibility seems to work OK.  This issue did not exist on 4.8-dev4.


### Steps to reproduce

1. Launch Godot 4.8-dev5
2. Click +Create button.
3. Choose target folder and click Create button.
4. Crash

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A
dup.author: PrismaticRealms

dup.title: Android: (Stack Trace) Crash - RenderingDeviceDriverVulkan::compute_pipeline_create()
dup.body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.7.2.stable

### System information

Samsung a04, Android 14

### Issue description

We're seeing some crashes in Play Console on 2 specific Android devices so far.

Godot 4.7.2.stable, Mobile renderer.

Device 1: Samsung Galaxy A04 (samsung a04), Android 14 (SDK 34)
Device 2: Motorola moto g55 5G (motorola taipei), Android 16 (SDK 36)

I have **not** seen this on any of the devices I have available on my own (Samsung Galaxy S9+ and Google Pixel 9a)., and the vast majority of our user base has seemingly not seen/reported this either.


We have 2 different issues in Play Console, but I believe they might be the same issue given the function signature displayed, although different crash "type" (SIGSEGV vs SIGABRT):

orig.title: Android / Vulkan Mobile crash on MediaTek MT6765 and MT6855 (PowerVR GE8320 and BXM 8-256) when creating pipeline for scene shader (analytics report)
orig.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.5.stable
- Reproducible in 4.6.stable
- Reproducible in https://github.com/akien-mga/godot/releases/tag/4.5.1.stable%2Bvulkan_mobile_fixes which is 4.5.1.stable + cherry-picks of Vulkan Mobile fixes made by @blueskythlikesclouds recently (https://github.com/akien-mga/godot/compare/4.5.1-stable...4.5.1.stable+vulkan_mobile_fixes).

### System information

Various Android devices (versions 10 to 15) with Mediatek MT6765 (ImgTech PowerVR GE8320) or Mediatek MT6855 (4x ImgTech BXM 8-256)

Checking logs from the previous Spooky Express build on 4.5.stable, here's the full list of affected SoC on a bigger sample of devices:
- Mediatek MT6765 (PowerVR GE8320)
- Mediatek MT6765V/XBA (PowerVR GE8320)
- Mediatek MT6762 (PowerVR GE8320)
- Mediatek MT6762V/CA (PowerVR GE8320)
- Mediatek MT6762V/CB (PowerVR GE8320)
- Mediatek MT6855 (4x BXM 8-256)
- Mediatek MT6779p90 (2x PowerVR GM9446)
- Mediatek MT6779p95 (2x PowerVR GM9446)
- Mediatek MT8768N (PowerVR GE8320)
- Spreadtrum SC9863A (PowerVR GE8322)
- Spreadtrum T603 (PowerVR GE8322)

160 affected users in 8 days.

### Issue description

This is a crash seen in the wild on a number of devices with @Draknek's [Spooky Express](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=express.spooky) (10k+ install base).

We're seeing the following crash stacktrace affecting devices with either Mediatek MT6765 SoC (Imagination Technologies PowerVR GE8320) or MT6855 (BXM 8-256), on multiple recent Android versions.

dup.title: Export to Mac App Store missing required LSMinimumSystemVersion key in info.plist
dup.body:
### Tested versions

4.7.2

### System information

macOS 26.6.2

### Issue description

When exporting for submission to the Apple Mac App Store Godot generates a nice signed .pkg package for you if you select the Distribution type "App Store" that you can then submit via the Transporter app.

However, it seems the generated app bundle info.plist is missing a LSMinimumSystemVersion key that is required for apps submitted to the App Store. So the packages will be rejected in Transporter. 

Looking at the info.plist generated by Godot it now contains:
```
<key>LSMinimumSystemVersionByArchitecture</key>
	<dict>
		<key>arm64</key>
		<string>13.00</string>
		<key>x86_64</key>
		<string>11.00</string>
	</dict>
``` 

Which is probably meant to replace LSMinimumSystemVersion. However, it seems the App Store package analysis specifically requires LSMinimumSystemVersion to be present. So if you just add
```
<key>LSMinimumSystemVersion</key>
<string>13.0</string>
```
It will accept the package. It seems a little redundant to have both, but for the app store submission it seems to be required at least for now.

### Steps to reproduce

- Have a Godot project
- Export for macOS , Distribution type App Store (Requires you have app store distribution certificates/identifiers, profiles etc)
- Once you have your output .pkg use the Transporter app to upload this to the Apple App Store (or just use the Verify function, that does the verification without uploading it)
- Get error about missing LSMinimumSystemVersion key in info.plist

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Not project specific

orig.title: macOS App Store export missing LSMinimumSystemVersion, causing Transporter rejection
orig.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in Godot 4.7 .NET

### System information

macOS 26.6.2 2022 MacBook Air M2 8GB

### Issue description

A macOS project exported by Godot for Mac App Store distribution as a signed `.pkg` cannot be uploaded using Apple's Transporter because the generated `Info.plist` does not contain the top-level `LSMinimumSystemVersion` key.

Transporter rejects the package with:

> The LSMinimumSystemVersion key must be present in the Info.plist file when submitting a macOS app.

Godot does generate `LSMinimumSystemVersionByArchitecture`, for example:

```xml
<key>LSMinimumSystemVersionByArchitecture</key>
<dict>
    <key>arm64</key>
    <string>13.0</string>
    <key>x86_64</key>
    <string>11.0</string>
</dict>
```

but it does not generate `LSMinimumSystemVersion`.

Adding the following manually through **Application > Additional Plist Content** in the macOS export preset resolves the Transporter validation error:

```xml
<key>LSMinimumSystemVersion</key>
<string>11.0</string>
```

This appears to be a regression introduced by #95885 ("[macOS] Use per-architecture min. OS version for export.").

Prior to that PR, the macOS export template contained both:

```xml
<key>LSMinimumSystemVersion</key>
<string>$min_version</string>

<key>LSMinimumSystemVersionByArchitecture</key>
...
```

#95885 removed the top-level `LSMinimumSystemVersion` when introducing separate minimum versions for arm64 and x86_64.

The current per-architecture settings are useful, but Apple's current App Store Transporter validation still requires `LSMinimumSystemVersion` to be present when submitting a macOS application.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a Godot project.
2. Add a macOS export preset.
3. Configure it for App Store distribution, including:
   - App Store distribution type
   - signing identity
   - installer identity
   - provisioning profile
4. Configure the minimum macOS versions in the export preset.
5. Export the project as a signed `.pkg`.
6. Upload the `.pkg` using Apple's Transporter app.
7. Transporter rejects the package with:

   `The LSMinimumSystemVersion key must be present in the Info.plist file when submitting a macOS app.`

orig.title: `TypedArray<>` does not export C# bindings correctly if the type is `int64_t` or `uint64_t`
orig.body:
### Tested versions

v4.2.1.stable.mono.official [b09f793f5]
v4.3.stable.mono.official [77dcf97d8]
v4.5.1.stable.mono.official [f62fdbde1]

### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable.mono (f62fdbde1) - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 3 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8108) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-10900K CPU @ 3.70GHz (20 threads) - 31.85 GiB memory

### Issue description

I first noticed this bug when I had to use `PhysicsTestMotionParameters3D::set_exclude_objects`, which accepts what should be an array of `ObjectID`. This is not a variant type, so the current C++ implementation exports it as `TypedArray<uint64_t>`.

The problem arises when the C# version of the API is created. The property (and its getter/setter) are incorrectly interpreted as `Array<int>` rather than `Array<ulong>`, which is particularly egregious when it comes to `ObjectID`.

Still, this is not exactly urgent even if it does make that method effectively unusable. The `exclude_bodies` property which accepts `Array<Rid>` is the better choice *basically* every time. Regardless, I've implemented a temporary stopgap in my fork by changing it to a variant `Array`. I'm not aware of any cleaner solutions, but if there is one I can implement until an official fix is released, do let me know.

Thank you.

StandardMaterial, PanoramaSkyMaterial (probably more) - Atlas Textures dont remotely work here, they default to just showing the source fully without region


### Steps to reproduce

Create an image Source create 2 atlasTextures A and B
set A's atlas to Source, set B's atlas to A
Create a new scene with CPU or GPU particles, set texture to A or B and observe the particles

dup.title: Commented out `{` and end-of-line comments inhibit Shader Editor Previews
dup.body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in: 4.7.stable ### System information Godot v4.7.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon R7 Graphics (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 27.20.20913.2000) - AMD A12-9720P RADEON R7, 12 COMPUTE CORES 4C+8G (4 threads) - 7.46 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description When using `FRAGCOORD` (or any other value) in a `.gdshader` after a line that as a commented out curly bracket open, the preview displays a completely different value than before, and seems to default to a `vec4(1.0)` display. _Shows the difference between //{ and only // on the line. Keep in mind that shader previews generally ONLY update AFTER a preview was toggled, and do not automatically refresh when a shader line is changed. The fact that removing the bracket and space from the commented line DID make the previews update is completely unexpected behavior._ I am unsure whether this means the actual data that is returned is different as well. It seems more likely that the parsing for for-loops goes incorrectly, which causes the data to be reset to a default value, since previewing *inside* a for loop is not allowed, or that the assignment isn't properly singled out and turned into a color to display. Ran into this after commenting out a `for (i = 0; i < 10; i++) {` line to use the previews to debug my shader. Both `// {` and `// }` result in the same outcome, and which values is previewed does not seem to matter. Even constants such as `vec4(1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0)` have this issue. The line `// {}` does **not** seem to cause this issue. Might be a similar issue to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/120472. since comments being parsed seems to be an underlying trend in Shader Editor issues. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a new Spatial Shader in a ShaderMaterial 2. Apply the ShaderMaterial to a 3D object 3. Select the 3D object 4. Add the following code to the shader ```GDShader void fragment() { vec4 original = FRAGCOORD; // a comment vec4 pre = FRAGCOORD; // { vec4 post = FRAGCOORD; // Incorrect display } ``` 5. Toggle on the previews for all the 3 assignments 6. Any assignment of `FRAGCOORD` after the commented out `{` will display a value of vec4(1.0), while any before do not. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A

orig.title: Comments cause incorrect text shader line preview
orig.body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in: 4.8.dev custom build [95baa6f29], 4.7.stable.official. ### System information Godot v4.8.dev (95baa6f29) - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 Ti Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6109) - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-1240P (16 threads) - 31.71 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description Shader line previews do not handle comments correctly. When an assignment has a trailing `//` comment, its preview may incorrectly include the following assignment and display that assignment's result instead. Comments containing braces or function-like code can also affect scope detection and brace counting, producing malformed preview shaders and compilation errors. Inline and multiline `/* ... */` comments can prevent otherwise valid assignments from being recognized. For example, in `simple_bug_test.gdshader`, previewing the statements at line 4/6/8 may display the result of the following blue assignment: or fail with: ```text SHADER ERROR: Expected constant, function, uniform or varying. ERROR: Shader compilation failed. ERROR: Parameter "version" is null. ``` Previewing an assignment with certain trailing comments may instead display: ```text Previewed line must contain an assignment. ``` ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open the attached project. 2. Open `simple_bug_test.gdshader` or `complex_bug_test.gdshader`. 3. Place the caret on one of the assignments containing a comment. 4. Press F9 to enable a shader line preview. 5. Observe that: - The preview may display the result of the following assignment. - An assignment may not be recognized. - Comments containing braces or function-like code may cause shader compilation errors. 6. Remove the comments and repeat the preview. 7. Observe that the preview works correctly. P.S. If the preview appears correct after opening or saving the file, place the caret on any line and press F9 twice. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [shader-preview-bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/29657669/shader-preview-bug.zip)

```
}
```

orig.title: [4.7] mbedTLS: Always use Godot's OS as entropy source
orig.body:
mbedTLS < 4 provides internal platform functions to seed the random number generator with entropy from the OS.

Historically we have been relying on this when the mbedTLS module is enabled, while we have been using the OS::get_entropy when building without the module.

Given we had issues on some platform with the built-in implementation, this commit forces the use of OS::get_entropy in all cases (module or not).

This is already the case when using mbedTLS 4 (Godot 4.8+).

Fixes #121717 (I can't really test it on the offending devices sadly).

regression from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/121055
orig.author: Faless

**Issue description**
After updating to Godot Android Editor 4.7.1 Stable, the application takes an unusually long time to start.

Every time I launch the editor, it stays on the Android splash screen for about **2 minutes** before the Godot logo finally appears. In previous versions, startup was much faster.

The issue occurs before the editor interface is displayed, so no project needs to be opened.

2. Wait for the application to start.

The Godot logo should appear within a few seconds after the Android splash screen, as it did in previous versions.

**Actual result**
The application remains on the Android splash screen for approximately **2 minutes** before the Godot logo appears and the editor finally opens.

**Reproducibility**
Always (100%).

**Additional information**

* This issue only occurs in **Godot Android Editor 4.7.1 Stable**.
* Previous versions (such as **4.7 Stable**) started normally and much faster on the same device.
* No project needs to be opened for the issue to occur.
* The issue happens before the editor UI is displayed.

dup.title: TileSet animation property sections collapse after adding or editing frames
dup.body: ### Tested versions Reproduced in Godot v4.7.1.stable.official. Tested in Godot v4.6.1.stable.official, where the issue does not occur. This appears to be a regression introduced between 4.6.1 and 4.7.1. ### System information Godot v4.7.1.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 3 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9186) - AMD Ryzen 7 5800X 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 31.88 Gio memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description When editing an animated tile in the TileSet editor, the expanded property sections collapse after every change. For example, after expanding the `Animation` section and then the `Frames` section, adding a new frame causes both sections to collapse. The same thing happens when changing the duration of an animation frame. As a result, the user has to reopen `Animation`, then `Frames`, after every modification. This makes editing tile animations unnecessarily slow and frustrating. A short gif is attached to this issue to demonstrate the behavior. The issue is easily reproducible in the TileSet editor. I have not verified whether the same behavior also occurs in other parts of the Inspector. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a new project. 2. Create a new TileSet resource. 3. Create a tile and enable animation. 4. Expand the `Animation` section. 5. Expand the `Frames` section. 6. Add a new animation frame. 7. Observe that both sections collapse. 8. Expand them again and change the duration of any frame. 9. Observe that the sections collapse again. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A

Testing a project exported with Godot 4.7 it seems the update has broken something with the metal driver initiation on older systems. orig.title: Only propagate physics server transforms when different
orig.body:
Fixes #117852.
Fixes #118077.
Supersedes #117964.

This changes the physics server state synchronization for `RigidBody2D`, `RigidBody3D` and `PhysicalBone3D` to check if the transform has actually changed before calling `set_global_transform` with said transform.

`RigidBody2D` was seemingly trying to do this for frozen/kinematic bodies already, by just ignoring transform updates completely, but doing so results in transform desync (#118077).

Note that this isn't strictly needed for `PhysicalBone3D`, since it doesn't currently support freezing, but that's something that definitely should be added at some point, at which point this fix will kick in there as well.

I suspect this change is also applicable to `AnimatableBody*D`, as there seems to be issues with redundant `NOTIFICATION_TRANSFORM_CHANGED` notifications when `sync_to_physics` is enabled, but I'm having trouble reasoning about potential regressions there, and it's not as pressing of an issue, so I'm leaving them alone for now.

orig.title: C#: Intermittent Handle is not initialized when instantiating a PackedScene referencing a cached CompressedTexture2D
orig.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in Godot v4.6.dev2.mono

### System information

Ubuntu 25.04 25.04 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Mesa Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics (RPL-P) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-13900H (20 threads) - 30.51 GiB memory

### Issue description

When a scene that references a texture is instantiated in C#, the engine consistently throws an exception (under specific project layout) inside ScriptManagerBridge.SwapGCHandleForType, saying “Handle is not initialized.”

The error appears to happen when a cached native Resource is reused, and the engine tries to convert a released weak GCHandle into a strong one.
When attaching a debugger, the issue disappears.



### Steps to reproduce

approximate sequence:

// Step 1
var texture = ResourceLoader.Load<CompressedTexture2D>("res://t.png");
// ...
// Step 2
var scene = ResourceLoader.Load<PackedScene>("res://s.tscn"); // s.tscn has a Sprite2D using t.png

// Step 3
scene.Instantiate();

Error Output

ERROR: System.InvalidOperationException: Handle is not initialized.
   at System.Runtime.InteropServices.GCHandle.FromIntPtr(IntPtr value)
   at Godot.Bridge.ScriptManagerBridge.SwapGCHandleForType(IntPtr oldGCHandlePtr, IntPtr* outNewGCHandlePtr, godot_bool createWeak) in /root/godot/modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/Bridge/ScriptManagerBridge.cs:line 1280
   at: void Godot.NativeInterop.ExceptionUtils.LogException(System.Exception) (/root/godot/modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/NativeInterop/ExceptionUtils.cs:113)
   C# backtrace (most recent call first):
       [0] void Godot.GD.PushError(string) (/root/godot/modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/GD.cs:366)
       [1] void Godot.NativeInterop.ExceptionUtils.LogException(System.Exception) (/root/godot/modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/NativeInterop/ExceptionUtils.cs:113)
       [2] Godot.NativeInterop.godot_bool Godot.Bridge.ScriptManagerBridge.SwapGCHandleForType(nint, System.IntPtr*, Godot.NativeInterop.godot_bool) (/root/godot/modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Core/Bridge/ScriptManagerBridge.cs:1280)
       [3] void Godot.NativeInterop.NativeFuncs.godotsharp_method_bind_ptrcall(nint, nint, System.Void**, System.Void*) (/root/godot/modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Godot.SourceGenerators.Internal/Godot.SourceGenerators.Internal.UnmanagedCallbacksGenerator/Godot.NativeInterop.NativeFuncs.generated.cs:380)
       [4] Godot.GodotObject Godot.NativeCalls.godot_icall_1_79(nint, nint, int) (/root/godot/modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Generated/NativeCalls.cs:703)
       [5] Godot.Node Godot.PackedScene.Instantiate(Godot.PackedScene+GenEditState) (/root/godot/modules/mono/glue/GodotSharp/GodotSharp/Generated/GodotObjects/PackedScene.cs:130)

At the point of failure (_instance_binding_reference_callback):

gchandle.get_intptr() = 0x0
gchandle.is_weak() = true
gchandle.is_released = true
script_binding.owner->get_class() = CompressedTexture2D
refcount = 2
Object::cast_to<Resource>(script_binding.owner)->get_path() = res://t.png

Hypothesis:

The texture (CompressedTexture2D) is loaded from C#, creating a managed wrapper whose weak handle is stored in the native resource cache.

Later, the managed wrapper is GC-collected, releasing its handle, while the native resource stays cached.

When the scene referencing the same texture is instantiated, the cache reuses that native resource and attempts to upgrade the old weak handle to a strong one.

Because the handle pointer is now invalid (0), GCHandle.FromIntPtr throws instead of creating a new managed wrapper.


When attempting to reproduce this behavior in other projects,

scene.Instantiate() never attempts to perform a GCHandle swap (_instance_binding_reference_callback is not called at all for the texture owned by the Sprite2D).
In the affected project, however, instantiating the same kind of scene does trigger a handle swap for the CompressedTexture2D (res://t.png),


### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

The issue always occurs under the same build of the my project, but may disappear if the code layout changes slightly
Cannot reproduce in a minimal reproduction project, even with similar resource setup
Disappears when a managed debugger is attached

orig.title: Illegal recursion allowed through PackedScene
orig.body:
### Godot version

v4.1.2.stable.official [399c9dc39]

### System information

Godot v4.1.2.stable - Windows 10.0.22621 - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 Ti (NVIDIA; 30.0.15.1216) - AMD Ryzen 9 5950X 16-Core Processor (32 Threads)

### Issue description

When you create a Resource that `@export` a variable, it will not allow a circular reference through other Resources.

However, you can circumvent this and break Godot by creating the circular reference through a PackedScene such that the structure looks like the following:

ExampleResource:
`@export my_scene: PackedScene`

MyScene
`@export my_resource: ExampleResource`

i.e.
ExampleResource -> MyScene -> ExampleResource

You can save and run the project, but "MyScene" thinks that my_resource is null even if it is set in the editor. When you exit the project and try to re-open it, you get the following error:
```
  scene/resources/resource_format_text.cpp:283 - res://MainScene.tscn:8 - Parse Error: 
  Failed loading resource: res://MainScene.tscn. Make sure resources have been imported by opening the project in the editor at least once.
  editor/editor_data.cpp:626 - Index p_idx = 1 is out of bounds (edited_scene.size() = 1).
```

From this point, you can no longer open MyScene or ExampleResource.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a script that extends `Resource` (e.g. MyResource)
2. Have that script export a variable of type PackedScene
3. Create a Scene (e.g. named MyScene)
4. Attach a script to the scene that exports a variable of the same type as the resource you created above
5. Create a new instance of the resource (e.g. MyResourceInstance)
6. In MyResourceInstance, attach MyScene to the exported variable field
7. in MyScene, attach MyResourceInstance to the exported variable field

### Minimal reproduction project

[ResourceRecursion.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/13184747/ResourceRecursion.zip)

dup.body:

Godot v4.8.dev.mono (d76b83872) - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2060 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.5599) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-10750H CPU @ 2.60GHz (12 threads) - 15.76 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

Setup:
- Have C# tool script had been compiled before
- Modify the script to have uncompiled changes that contain new property definitions
- Values for these properties exist in `PackedScene` or `Resource` file
- Build scripts

Result: 
- Property data is lost for any instances currently loaded by the editor. 
- Saving without reopening the scene or project removes the data from file

Expected:
- Property data is loaded correctly in editor
- Saving doesn't remove data

This can happen normally by pulling changes from source control.

Non-tool scripts don't have this issue since the placeholder script instance has tolerance for missing property definitions while in editor. `CSharpInstance` doesn't look like it does the same, so missing property definitions means immediately dropping the data.

For anyone else who experiences this issue, this can be worked around in a few ways
1. Building the C# code before opening the project
2. Building the C# code with the editor
   - If new properties were only to `Node` classes, reopening scenes without saving should load the data back
   - If new properties were in `Resource` classes, reopen the whole editor

Maybe related to #109698 

### Steps to reproduce

- Open the project in the MRP which is in the folder `empty`
- Build scripts
- Uncomment any property in `Test.cs` and save
- Copy `Main.tscn` from the root of the MRP folder into the project

The project is now in a similar state to having pulled changes from source control
- Build scripts
- Notice the property values in editor are default values instead of what's in the copied `Main.tscn`
- Notice saving doesn't add property values to `Main.tscn` in the project

orig.title: Custom properties of a C# Tool class reset when .NET project built while scene is open
orig.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.4.1.stable.mono.official [49a5bc7b6]

### System information

Godot v4.4.1.stable.mono - macOS Sequoia (15.6.0) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon Pro 5300M - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-9750H CPU @ 2.60GHz (12 threads)

### Issue description

Custom properties (defined with overridden `_Get`/`_Set`/`_GetPropertyList`) on a C# Tool class (required to edit custom properties in the editor) can have their values reset in the scene, if the .NET project is built _while the scene is open_.

If the .NET project is built from the editor while the scene is open, only custom properties backed directly by a top level field in the class will retain their customized values.
Custom properties whose values are really stored inside some sub-object will be reset.

All custom properties are populated correctly when a scene is first opened, as when loading the scene Godot calls the custom `_Set` implementation for such properties (after calling the constructor), passing `_Set` the persisted property values from the scene file. This seems like expected behaviour here, and is already working correctly when the scene is opened from disk.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open sample project
2. **Close** the default scene
3. Click _**Build Project**_ button
4. Open `test3d.tscn`
5. Node `Test3d/MyThingyCs` has custom properties:
    * `MyName` - stored directly in public string field on `MyThingy`
    * `MyBuggyName` - stored inside a private field `MyThingyCs._myBuggyNameData.MyBuggyName` - `MyThingy._myBuggyNameData` value is constructed in the `MyThingyCs` constructor
6. `MyName` and `MyBuggyName` are both currently set to "Graham" (from `.tscn` file).
Custom `_Set` method is only called to set `MyBuggyName` (see console log), `MyName` property is somehow set in some other way.
7. Make some minor edit to `src/MyThingy.cs` (eg. add extra newline) so that it must be rebuilt
8. While `test3d.tscn` is still open, click _**Build Project**_ button
9. Note that `MyBuggyName` property is now reset to default value "Bob"

I tested same behaviour for custom properties of a GDScript file, stored in an underlying .NET object (see `my_thingy_gd.gd` that stores it's custom properties in `MyThingyCs.cs`) and it has the same effect.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[godotcscustomsetter_2025-08-17_21-04-40.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21823335/godotcscustomsetter_2025-08-17_21-04-40.zip)

dup.title: DynamicFont: Mixing CJK characters with brackets causes excessive DrawCalls due to font atlas pagination
dup.body:
### Tested versions

## Issue Description

When using DynamicFont to render text that mixes CJK (Chinese/Japanese/Korean) characters with brackets (both full-width `（）` and half-width `()`), Godot generates excessive DrawCalls even with a small number of labels.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a project with a CJK font (e.g., simsun.ttc)
2. Create a LoopContainer or VBoxContainer
3. Add 10-20 labels with text like: `"物品名称（带括号）"` or `"Item (with brackets)"`
4. Observe DrawCalls in the debugger (can reach 100-200+ DrawCalls)

## Expected Behavior

DrawCalls should remain low regardless of whether brackets are mixed with CJK characters.

## Actual Behavior

DrawCalls explode when CJK characters and brackets are mixed:
- 10 labels without brackets: ~20-30 DrawCalls
- 10 labels with CJK + brackets: ~100-200 DrawCalls

## Root Cause Analysis

Godot's DynamicFont uses a font atlas for rendering glyphs. When the atlas page is full, it creates a new page, and each page requires additional DrawCalls. The issue is that:

1. CJK characters are rendered to one atlas page
2. Brackets (both full-width and half-width) are rendered to a different atlas page
3. Each text switch between these pages triggers additional DrawCalls

## Workaround (Current)

```gdscript
# Preload characters by rendering all needed characters at startup
func preload_chars():
    var vp = SubViewport.new()
    vp.size = Vector2i(2048, 512)
    add_child(vp)
    
    var label = Label.new()
    label.add_theme_font_override("font", font)
    label.text = "所有需要预加载的字符（括号）()"  # Include both CJK and brackets
    vp.add_child(label)
    
    await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw
    await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw
    vp.queue_free()
```

## Suggested Solution

1. Add a `FontFile.preload_chars(chars: String, size: int)` method to preload specific characters to the font atlas at runtime

2. Add a `FontFile.page_size` property that can be set at runtime (currently read-only after loading)

3. Document the font atlas pagination behavior and provide best practices for CJK text rendering

## Environment

- Godot version: 4.6.x
- Renderer: Forward+
- Platform: Windows/Linux/macOS
- Font: DynamicFont with .ttc/.ttf file

## Tags

`rendering` `font` `dynamicfont` `drawcalls` `performance` `cjk`

### System information

- Godot version: 4.6.x - Renderer: Forward+ - Platform: Windows/Linux/macOS - Font: DynamicFont with .ttc/.ttf file

### Issue description

When using DynamicFont to render text that mixes CJK (Chinese/Japanese/Korean) characters with brackets (both full-width `（）` and half-width `()`), Godot generates excessive DrawCalls even with a small number of labels.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a project with a CJK font (e.g., simsun.ttc)
2. Create a LoopContainer or VBoxContainer
3. Add 10-20 labels with text like: `"物品名称（带括号）"` or `"Item (with brackets)"`
4. Observe DrawCalls in the debugger (can reach 100-200+ DrawCalls)

dup.title: Severe Frame Drops/Freezing with High Polling Rate Mouse (MCHOSE L7 PRO at 4000Hz/8000Hz) - Input Accumulation Fails
dup.body:
### Tested versions

Godot 4.5 / Godot 4.6 (Testing branches)

### System information

OS: Windows 11 / Windows 10 Mouse: MCHOSE L7 PRO (Running at 4000Hz / 8000Hz polling rate via official driver)

### Issue description

When using a high polling rate mouse (4000Hz or 8000Hz), moving the mouse quickly causes massive CPU spikes and severe frame drops, sometimes completely freezing the main thread.

I initially encountered this while developing my 2D game BOP&POP, where GUI node traversal was suspected. However, the exact same issue persists even in a completely empty project.

Important Note: I have already tried all standard workarounds, but none resolved the underlying stutter:

Input.use_accumulated_input = true is enabled.

Agile Event Flushing is disabled in Project Settings.

physics_object_picking is set to false.

V-Sync is disabled and FPS is capped to monitor refresh rate.

Even setting Input.set_deferred("mouse_mode", Input.MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED) or explicitly calling get_viewport().set_input_as_handled() in _input() to manually throttle the events does not fix it.

It appears the bottleneck is entirely at the OS message pump level (WM_INPUT/Message Queue) or DisplayServer before it even reaches the GDScript input callbacks. The engine struggles to handle the sheer volume of hardware interrupts from modern 8K mice.

Steps to reproduce:

Set the physical mouse polling rate to 4000Hz or 8000Hz via its driver software.

Open the attached empty minimal reproduction project.

Run the project and move the mouse rapidly across the screen.

Observe the severe FPS drop and frame time spikes in the profiler.

### Steps to reproduce

Set the physical mouse polling rate to 4000Hz or 8000Hz via its driver software.

Open the attached empty minimal reproduction project.

Run the project and move the mouse rapidly across the screen.

Observe the severe FPS drop and frame time spikes in the profiler.

Pseudocode referred to in description
``` C#
[ExportGroup(Group1)]
```

When calling get_property_list on a class with a C# script running in the editor. The order is as you world expect
- builtin properties...

- property2 

but in an exported build the property list will reverse the script properties
 - builtin properties...
 - property2
 - property1
 - Group1
 
in modules/mono/csharp_script.cpp there's a couple of snippets like the one below. where in exported builds push_front is called when iterating through member_info.
``` C++
#ifdef TOOLS_ENABLED
	for (const PropertyInfo &prop : script->exported_members_cache) {
		props.push_back(prop);
	}
#else
	for (const KeyValue<StringName, PropertyInfo> &E : script->member_info) {
		props.push_front(E.value);
	}
#endif
```

### Steps to reproduce

Run the project in the editor look at console output or onscreen text. Then export the project and run the exported project.

### Issue description

### Short Version 

C# performance seems to have suffer due to StringName equality checks in generated methods like `HasGodotClassMethod `and `InvokeGodotClassMethod`

### Long Version

I noticed that performance in my game drops sharply with a large number of nodes doing basically nothing. So I created a small repro project to try and explain what I have observed. 

In the repro project we have a very simple script that toggles a Label from `a` to `b` every second. This is done in a `_process` callback in both GDScript and C#. We instantiate 1000 instances of the label to simulate a large number of nodes. At a too large number (10000) the project is very slow, so differences between GDScript and C# are not noticable.

![label_gd_3 5 3](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/2500134/19441c3c-d916-4f06-add4-ea79cea9b13b)
C#
![label_mono_3 5 3](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/2500134/b3be0155-6937-42a4-9626-73327a343220)

I ran a dotTrace using Rider to try and figure out what is going on, and here are the results for 4.2.1
![test_cache_4_2_1_trace](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/2500134/acbcb2d8-e8db-43b7-9b5d-59f42ec5b8dc)

it's here I first noticed the equality checks on StringNames taking up a bit of time. Which led me to assume that the if-else chain in the `HasGodotClassMethod `and `InvokeGodotClassMethod` might be part of the problem.

I experimented in modifying the ScriptGenerators to use cached method calls instead of comparison checks https://github.com/TheOrioli/godot/commit/c291f64568899bb17d300655aa6a57179ae91cb0 and it seems to provide a bit of a speedup in my main project, but I do not know how to change those methods for built-in godot types. 

You can see a small pyramid in the flame graph disappear under `TestLabel.InvokeGodotClassMethod` 
![test_cache_custom_trace](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/2500134/a6d22a8f-dd84-465a-a952-fcbe2b5520d0)

I there is definitely something here, and there is potential to eliminate all those comparison checks which should provide a speedup and bring C# closer to GDScript in performance. I am hoping someone more familiar with the codebase can help out in figuring this out and testing more properly.

This behavior unfortunately means that making lots of small scripts in C# will lead to unintended performance degradation in games.

### Steps to reproduce

- Open repro project
- Run `main.tscn` with the Node property "Use CSharp" set to false
- Observe FPS monitors
- Run `main.tscn` with the Node property "Use CSharp" set to true
- Observe FPS monitors

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

4.3-dev4, contains screenshots from above in folder [test_mono_method_cache.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/14511773/test_mono_method_cache.zip)

dup.title: even when use_external_editor is set to true and exec_path / exec_flags are correctly configured.
dup.body:
### Tested versions

4.6.stable.mono (official)

### System information

Windows 11, VS Code 1.124.2 (x64), .NET / C# project

### Issue description

When Script Editor is unchecked in Manage Editor Features (the toolbar toggle dropdown), Godot silently ignores all script-click interactions — including launching the configured external editor — even when use_external_editor is set to true and exec_path / exec_flags are correctly configured.

Expected behavior:
Unchecking Script Editor should only hide/disable the built-in script editor panel. The external editor (configured in Editor Settings → Text Editor → External) should still be launched when clicking a script, since the user has explicitly opted into using an external tool.

Actual behavior:
Clicking any script resource in the FileSystem dock or Scene tree does nothing. No error, no toast, no VS Code window — the click is silently dropped.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open any Godot 4.6 project (C# or GDScript).
2. Go to Editor → Editor Settings → Text Editor → External:
✅ Use External Editor
Exec Path: path to Code.exe (or any valid editor)
Exec Flags: --goto {file}:{line}:{col}
3. Confirm external editor works by clicking a script → VS Code opens.
4. In the toolbar, click the Manage Editor Features dropdown and uncheck Script Editor.
5. Click any script again → nothing happens.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Why this is confusing
Setting | User expects | Actually happens
-- | -- | --
Script Editor unchecked | Built-in editor hidden; external editor still works | ALL script interactions silently ignored
Use External Editor ✅ | External editor always invoked | Only when Script Editor is also checked

The Script Editor toggle functions as a global gatekeeper for all script interactions, not just the built-in panel. But the name Script Editor is read by most users as "the built-in script editor panel", making it natural to turn off when using an external editor — which then breaks the very thing they're trying to use.

Workaround
Keep Script Editor checked in Manage Editor Features, even when using an external editor.

Minimal reproduction project
Any project with a script file attached to a node. No custom code needed.

Actual behavior: The AreaLight3D shadow breaks into a smeared/incorrect artifact on the receiver. AreaLight3D result: OmniLight3D control result: ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a new 3D scene. 2. Set the renderer to Forward+. 3. Add an AreaLight3D and enable shadows. 4. Add a thick BoxMesh wall/box as occluder. 5. Add a BoxMesh wall/floor as shadow receiver. 6. Observe the broken/smeared shadow artifact on the receiver. 7. Replace the AreaLight3D with an OmniLight3D in the same scene. 8. Observe that the shadow is rendered correctly with OmniLight3D. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) Attached ZIP contains a minimal reproduction project. Contents: - `area_light_broken.tscn`: AreaLight3D with shadows enabled, showing the broken/smeared shadow artifact. - `omni_light_control.tscn`: Same setup using OmniLight3D, showing the expected correct shadow. The `.godot` folder is not included. [area_light_shadow_repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27310058/area_light_shadow_repro.zip)

orig.title: Exporting raw variant fields in scripts have different results in the editor inspector depending on how it's written
orig.body: ### Tested versions v4.5.beta7.official [4ebf67c12] ### System information Godot v4.5.beta7 - Windows 10 (build 19044) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL ES 3/ANGLE (Compatibility) - ANGLE (NVIDIA, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 Ti (0x00001C82) Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0, D3D11-31.0.15.4617) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-7700 CPU @ 3.60GHz (8 threads) - 15.93 GiB memory ### Issue description There are four different ways of writting the export for a raw variant field, and only one of them has the result a common user would expect when learning about the possibility of exporting raw variant fields: ```gdscript @export var m_with_type_without_default: Variant @export var m_with_type_with_default: Variant = 'm_with_type_with_default' @export var m_without_type_with_default = 'm_without_type_with_default' @export var m_without_type_without_default ``` Of these four usages, only the first one works, drawing a field that let you change the type ```gdscript @export var m_with_type_without_default: Variant ``` the next two exports become tied to the type of the initial value and do not let you change it. And lastly, the fourth type doesn't work at all, it raises a parser error with the message ```Error at (, ): Cannot use simple "@export" annotation with variable without type or initializer, since type can't be inferred.``` Even though I think most users whould expect all four syntaxes to be possible, the ones where a default value is provided are the most important, since it is pretty common for anyone to export a field with a default value, but none of the exports that have a default value allow changing the type. The exports with default value are being tied to the initial type but please note that I'm assigning the value with ```=```, not with ```:=```. We could even argue that makes sense for the value to the 'locked' when using ```:=``` but not when using ```=``` ### Steps to reproduce 1. create a new project in godot 4.5 beta 7 2. create a new scene 3. create a script in the root node 4. paste the code bellow in the script ```gdscript extends Node # this is the only one that allows changing the type in the inspector @export var m_with_type_without_default: Variant # this one does not allow changing the type in the inspector even though is typed as 'Variant' @export var m_with_type_with_default: Variant = 'm_with_type_with_default' # this one is untyped (and thus should be identical to typing as Variant) but also does not allow changing the type in the inspector @export var m_without_type_with_default = 'm_without_type_with_default' # this one could work but raises a parser error # @export var m_without_type_without_default # Error at (13, 1): Cannot use simple "@export" annotation with variable without type or initializer, since type can't be inferred. ``` Or just check the Main.tscn scene in the attached MRP ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [ExportVariantBug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22101500/ExportVariantBug.zip)

orig.title: Perform input validation on DAP requests
orig.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in `master` c3058391d7bd1a13481c393061c164c24ec99685

### System information

Arch Linux

### Issue description

> [!NOTE]
> This comes from initial analysis on https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/115188

The DAP backend does not perform a lot of input validation when it comes to parsing external JSON requests. In particular, after converting JSON to `Dictionary`, we tend to assume some keys will exist and fetch them directly, as they're guaranteed by the spec.

With recent changes such as 0be2a77156b62fab044da64687d9d0b456f47bbe, this reveals we are trying to fetch a key that does not exist:

```cpp
ERROR: Bug: Dictionary::operator[] used when there was no value for the given key "checksums". Please report.
   at: operator[] (core/variant/dictionary.cpp:136)
```

Likely occurring at:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/3f99bef808d32ebbbb5544e1f2e3d85d796bcd70/editor/debugger/debug_adapter/debug_adapter_types.h#L86-L96

While this doesn't seem to break debugging in any major way, it is a symptom of our lack of input validation.

LSP also found similar issues, and have been recently fixing them with a safer access to Dictionary keys ( #111684, #112128), so the same should be done here.

### Steps to reproduce

- Have a blank project with some code that hits a breakpoint:
```gdscript
func _ready() -> void:
    print("Here")  # <-- breakpoint
```
- Debug the project through an external editor
- Observe internal `Dictionary::operator[]` errors

N/A

orig.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in v4.7 beta1 snapshot, and v4.7.beta [d51d1ec68]
- Not reproducible in v4.6.2

### System information

Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9186) - AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 30.88 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

AnimationTree no longer produces any output (i.e. doesn't animate the character) if there are "errors" within the tree. I put that in quotes because, in some cases such as ours, those seeming errors are intentional. For example, leaving an Animation node with no specified animation because you'll be setting that animation from script dynamically (e.g. setting an animation tied to a gameplay state).

This was not the case in 4.6.2, so our experience was loading up the project in 4.7 and seeing our player character not animating anymore until we'd done sufficient inputs to "fill" our empty AnimationNodeAnimation's with animations. I didn't see anything like this in the breaking changes list, so I'm assuming this is unintentional.

In our example, we can workaround this by providing those Animation nodes with proper animations (discovering what was causing the issue was the bigger challenge) -- but this workaround makes it less intuitively obvious what's going on. The "empty" animation nodes (hooked up to a Transition or OneShot node) painted a much clearer picture that these are filled elsewhere (in script).

### Steps to reproduce

Within any working/used AnimationBlendTree, add an AnimationNodeAnimation node without specifying an animation. It doesn't need to be hooked up to anything.

In the provided MRP, you can observe the behavior change by opening it in 4.6.2 and seeing the ball animate, vs 4.7 beta1 seeing the ball not animate.

orig.title: Crashes on exit, when `GDScript` resources outlive `GDScriptLanguage`
orig.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.6.2.stable.official.71f334935
- Reproducible in 4.7.beta.custom_build.1f012286c

### System information

Fedora Linux

### Issue description

The GDScript module contains certain ref counted classes e.g. `GDScript`, `GDScriptFunctionState`. Due to how ref counting works it is absolutely possible, that those are referenced at some place, that is cleaned up after `GDScriptLanguage` (I use metadata on `Engine` for this. But there can be plenty of setups to hold references till very late in the engine shutdown.)

When `GDScript` or `GDScriptFunctionState` outlive `GDScriptLanguage` this leads to crashes later in the shutdown.

### Steps to reproduce

- Run the MRP (not from the editor, since it does not display shutdown issues apparently)
- Select the specific setup (what stays referenced beyond `GDScriptLanguage::finished`)
- Close the app
- This should lead to crash on exit

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[exit_crash.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27434960/exit_crash.zip)

(The project contains different setups, those all crash at the same point on master. However there is a second point of failure that only becomes relevant after fixing the first one, which is why multiple setups are included.)

dup.title: Dictionaries in ResourceFormatSaverText get reordered on save
dup.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in *every* version

### System information

N/A

### Issue description

in `core/variant/variant_parser.cpp` function `write`, dictionaries get their keys sorted. this leads to `.tres` files getting dictionary keys sorted. this breaks the promise in *sentence two* of the Dictionary documentation:

> Dictionaries will preserve the insertion order when adding new entries.

### Steps to reproduce

- have a Dictionary in anything saved with ResourceFormatSaverText
- reload it
- it's sorted now

orig.title: Forward+: TAA does not make the editor redraw until it has fully converged
orig.body:
*Related to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/54892, https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/54893 and https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/56723.*

### Godot version

4.0.alpha11, 4.3.dev4

### System information

Fedora 36, GeForce GTX 1080 (NVIDIA 510.68.02)

### Issue description

Temporal antialiasing (TAA) does not make the editor redraw until it has fully converged. This means that when toggling TAA or changing a setting that causes it to regenerate (such as resizing the editor viewport), it will have partially-converged appearance until you move the 3D camera around a bit (or cause the editor viewport to update somehow, e.g. by hovering controls).

We should resolve this by forcing the engine to redraw for 16 frames every time something is updated when both TAA and low processor mode are enabled.[^1] (16 frames is the duration of the Halton jitter sequence used by TAA.)

[^1]: We shouldn't just do this when the camera moves, as other objects being updated (such as a mesh's visibility being toggled) also requires the TAA to fully converge to look good – even if the camera doesn't move.

### Steps to reproduce

- Add some MeshInstance3Ds with BoxMeshes.
- Enable **Use TAA** in the Project Settings. Don't move the 3D editor camera for now. Notice the boxes' edges being aliased.
- Start moving the 3D editor camera *slowly* (use mouse wheel or hold <kbd>Alt</kbd> while using freelook). Notice how boxes' edges are smooth, at least until you stop moving.
- Enable **Update Continuously** in the Editor Settings to force the editor to redraw every frame. Notice how edges are smooth.

### Minimal reproduction project

N/A
orig.author: Calinou

dup.title: GDScriptInstance null-mutex SIGSEGV on shutdown when RefCounted stored in Engine metadata
dup.body:
# GDScriptInstance null-mutex SIGSEGV on shutdown when RefCounted stored in Engine metadata (or any core object destroyed after GDScriptLanguage) ## Tested versions - **Reproducible in:** 4.7.dev (master `c96e11965f`), 4.6.3.stable (official), 4.5.1.stable (confirmed via upstream #112480) - **Not reproducible in:** Not tested earlier — not a regression. The vulnerability has existed since `GDScriptLanguage` singleton-based `Mutex` locking was introduced in `GDScriptInstance::~GDScriptInstance()`. The bug triggers whenever any `GDScriptInstance` outlives `GDScriptLanguage` during `Main::cleanup()`. ## System information Linux (NixOS 25.11) — Vulkan (NVIDIA RTX 3090, nvidia-driver 560.35.03) — Godot 4.6.3.stable and 4.7.dev (master `c96e11965f`). The bug is **platform-independent** — confirmed on Windows by upstream #112480, which crashes at the same `pthread_mutex_lock()` call chain. No specific GPU, driver, or OS dependency. The crash occurs in C++ standard library mutex code (`mtx_do_lock` on MSVC, `pthread_mutex_lock` on Linux), making it inherently cross-platform. ## Issue description `Main::cleanup()` in `main/main.cpp` destroys the `GDScriptLanguage` module singleton **before** core types like `CoreBind::Engine` and their metadata. When any `GDScriptInstance` is still alive at this point (e.g., stored via the documented `Engine.set_meta()` API, or held in `AudioServer`'s internal safe-list), its destructor tries to lock `GDScriptLanguage::get_singleton()->mutex`. But the singleton was already set to `nullptr`, causing a `pthread_mutex_lock(nullptr)` → `SIGSEGV` → `abort()`. **Impact:** - Any addon or user code using `Engine.set_meta()` with a `RefCounted` script crashes on every shutdown - Any `class_name` GDScript extending `AudioStreamInteractive` with audio still playing crashes on shutdown (upstream #112480) - Any other mechanism that leaves a `GDScriptInstance` alive past SERVERS-level module cleanup will crash - This is a **latent vulnerability** in shutdown ordering: the engine must not crash during shutdown regardless of what GDScript objects are still alive
Shutdown order (annotated from main/main.cpp) ``` ScriptServer::finish_languages() ← GDScriptLanguage::finish() └── GDScript::clear() → static_variables cleared uninitialize_modules(MODULE_INITIALIZATION_LEVEL_SERVERS) └── memdelete(GDScriptLanguage) └── ~GDScriptLanguage() { singleton = nullptr; } *** GDScriptLanguage IS DEAD *** ... 80+ lines of server/singleton deletions ... unregister_core_types() └── memdelete(CoreBind::Engine) └── metadata HashMap::~HashMap() └── Variant::~Variant() → unref(RefCounted) └── refcount 0 → memdelete(RefCounted) └── ~GDScriptInstance() └── MutexLock(get_singleton()->mutex) *** CRASH: singleton is nullptr *** ```
The crash point is `modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp` in `GDScriptInstance::~GDScriptInstance()`: ```cpp GDScriptInstance::~GDScriptInstance() { MutexLock lock(GDScriptLanguage::get_singleton()->mutex); // SIGSEGV ... } ``` And the null singleton is set in `~GDScriptLanguage()`: ```cpp GDScriptLanguage::~GDScriptLanguage() { singleton = nullptr; // Member destructors run after this } ``` ## Steps to reproduce ### Required files (minimal reproduction — 3 files) Create a new Godot project with: **`project.godot`:** ``` [application] config/name="GDScriptInstance Shutdown Crash" run/main_scene="res://main.tscn" config/features=PackedStringArray("4.6") [autoload] repro_loader="*res://repro_loader.gd" ``` **`repro_loader.gd`:** ```gdscript extends Node func _ready(): var ref_script = load("res://repro_ref.gd") var _r = ref_script.new() print("Created RefCounted instance stored in Engine metadata") print("Calling quit() to trigger Main::cleanup()...") get_tree().quit() ``` **`repro_ref.gd`:** ```gdscript extends RefCounted func _init(): # Store self in Engine metadata. Engine's metadata HashMap is destroyed # during unregister_core_types() which runs AFTER GDScriptLanguage. Engine.set_meta("repro_shutdown_crash", self) print("Stored self in Engine.set_meta()") ``` Also create an empty `main.tscn` scene. ### Method 1: Game mode (simplest, ~2 seconds) ```bash godot4 --path . ``` A window opens briefly, then closes. Terminal shows: ``` REPRO [REF]: Stored self in Engine.set_meta() REPRO [AUTOLOAD]: Created RefCounted instance stored in Engine metadata REPRO [AUTOLOAD]: Calling quit() to trigger Main::cleanup()... ============================================================ handle_crash: Program crashed with signal 11 Engine version: Godot Engine v4.6.3.stable (e47e7067688e) Dumping the backtrace. Please include this when reporting the bug on: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues [1] /nix/store/.../libc.so.6(+0x3d6b0) [0x7f8a4ba2a6b0] (???) [2] pthread_mutex_lock+0x4 (??:?) [3] GDScriptInstance::~GDScriptInstance() (modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp:2066) [4] Object::_predelete() (core/object/object.cpp:1407) [5] void memdelete(RefCounted *) (core/object/object.h:840) [6] Variant::ObjData::unref() (core/variant/variant.cpp:234) [7] Object::~Object() (core/object/object.cpp:765) [8] unregister_core_types() (core/register_core_types.cpp:129) [9] Main::cleanup() (main/main.cpp:5391) [10] main() (platform/linuxbsd/godot_linuxbsd.cpp:76) -- END OF BACKTRACE -- ================================================================ Aborted (core dumped) ``` Exit code: `134` (SIGABRT). ### Method 2: Editor close ```bash godot4 --path . --editor # Close via File → Quit or Ctrl+Q ``` Same crash during editor shutdown (same backtrace, same exit code). ### Method 3: Headless export ```bash godot4 --headless --path . --export-release "Linux/X11" /tmp/export-test ``` Crash triggers after export completes, during `Main::cleanup()`.
Summary backtrace (call chain, all methods) ``` #5 pthread_mutex_lock() ← destroyed mutex #6 GDScriptInstance::~GDScriptInstance() ← ← crash point #7 Object::_predelete() #8 void memdelete() #9 Variant::ObjData::unref() ← Engine metadata #10 Object::~Object() ← Engine destructor #11 unregister_core_types() #12 main() ```
## Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [repro.zip](https://github.com/superherointj/godot/releases/download/repro-119799/repro.zip) 3-file project (plus editor plugin variant for editor/export methods): - `project.godot` — autoload + config - `repro_loader.gd` — creates RefCounted, calls `quit()` - `repro_ref.gd` — extends RefCounted, stores `self` in `Engine.set_meta()` - `addons/repro/` — EditorPlugin (needed for editor close and headless export methods) - `export_presets.cfg` — Linux export preset (needed for headless export method) No external assets or dependencies. ## Root cause analysis The fundamental problem is a **shutdown ordering vulnerability** in `Main::cleanup()`: - `ScriptServer::finish_languages()` is called first (clears script static variables) - `uninitialize_modules(MODULE_INITIALIZATION_LEVEL_SERVERS)` destroys `GDScriptLanguage` — sets `singleton = nullptr` - `unregister_core_types()` destroys `Engine` **after** GDScriptLanguage is dead - Engine's metadata holds a `Variant` referencing our `RefCounted`, which has a `GDScriptInstance` - `~GDScriptInstance()` tries to lock `get_singleton()->mutex` → `nullptr` → `SIGSEGV` See also upstream **#112480** (`AudioStreamInteractive` with `class_name` crashes via `AudioServer` destruction — same call chain, same root cause). ## Fix [PR #119800](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/119800) implements the following fix: ### Defensive null guard in `GDScriptInstance::~GDScriptInstance()` ```cpp GDScriptInstance::~GDScriptInstance() { if (GDScriptLanguage::get_singleton()) { MutexLock lock(GDScriptLanguage::get_singleton()->mutex); } ... } ``` After `GDScriptLanguage::finish()` has been called, no GDScript code executes. The mutex is not needed during single-threaded shutdown when all script data structures have already been cleared. A shutdown reordering approach (moving `uninitialize_modules(MODULE_INITIALIZATION_LEVEL_SERVERS)` after core types) was prototyped but **dropped** — ASan CI revealed a heap-use-after-free in SERVERS-level modules accessing memory freed during core type destruction. The null guard alone is sufficient.

orig.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.6.2.stable.official.71f334935
- Reproducible in 4.7.beta.custom_build.1f012286c

### System information

Fedora Linux

### Issue description

The GDScript module contains certain ref counted classes e.g. `GDScript`, `GDScriptFunctionState`. Due to how ref counting works it is absolutely possible, that those are referenced at some place, that is cleaned up after `GDScriptLanguage` (I use metadata on `Engine` for this. But there can be plenty of setups to hold references till very late in the engine shutdown.)

When `GDScript` or `GDScriptFunctionState` outlive `GDScriptLanguage` this leads to crashes later in the shutdown.

### Steps to reproduce

- Run the MRP (not from the editor, since it does not display shutdown issues apparently)
- Select the specific setup (what stays referenced beyond `GDScriptLanguage::finished`)
- Close the app
- This should lead to crash on exit

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[exit_crash.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27434960/exit_crash.zip)

(The project contains different setups, those all crash at the same point on master. However there is a second point of failure that only becomes relevant after fixing the first one, which is why multiple setups are included.)

orig.title: Renaming a scene file to convert between binary and text format throws errors and makes scene unloadable
orig.body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in `4.2`, `4.3`, `4.4`

### System information

Godot v4.3.stable - Windows 10.0.22631 - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1660 SUPER (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6109) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-10700F CPU @ 2.90GHz (16 Threads)

### Issue description

When you rename a scene file and change its extension in such a way that it changes implied format (from binary to text or vice versa), it doesn't actually change the contents of the file, and throws various errors (a little unpredictable depending if the file is open or which direction you're going). The resulting scene file is not openable.

![Screenshot 2024-09-12 140046](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4763d39e-a245-40d6-8cd7-da23930b128c)
![Screenshot 2024-09-12 140033](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/40d074f6-151f-41d7-b0d2-079a37a62e5e)
![Screenshot 2024-09-12 141138](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/29cf55da-5144-4807-b6e0-58d4c9cc13a5)
![Screenshot 2024-09-12 141332](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d922151d-3eea-422f-8666-7c7eb5a4a5d2)

The expected behaviour is that the scene should automatically re-save itself in the new intended format based on the extension, and should be openable after rename. It is possible to work around this issue with the following steps:
- Make sure the scene is open, and is dirty (`*` in the title bar)
- Rename the file to the new extension
- Choose `Save As` from the open scene, and _overwrite_ the newly renamed scene

The above should just happen automatically with the rename.

### Steps to reproduce

- Rename any `.tscn` scene to `.scn`, OR:
- Rename any `.scn` scene to `.tscn`

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A
